My name is Angela Mick, and I'm the Manager of Quality Management and Water Programs.
Every year we present reports to the owner and council to summarize the drinking water
system and to meet the regulatory requirements of the Safe Drinking Water Act.
When we have a new term of Council, we also bring forward the Operational Plan for re-endorsement
and to inform Council about their legislative responsibilities and to obtain commitment on
the water system.
These reports work together to ensure compliance and conformance of the drinking water system
and to ensure that the drinking water is safe.
The first report, the operational plan, consists of 21 elements including infrastructure renewal, risk assessment, emergency response, and communication.
Our standard operating procedures are high-level documents that describe the who, what, and when.
The work instructions are more detailed and describe the how.
There are over 300 documents including forms.
The Drinking Water Quality Management System, or DWQMS, is a living document and changes weekly.
We have a regulatory requirement to continually improve the system through audits, staff feedback, debriefs and suggestions.
Council re-endorsement of the plan shows owner commitment to the drinking water system.
We had our third party audit this fall for the DWQMS and they recommended recertification,
meaning we are in conformance and we are doing what we say we do in our procedures.
We completed a variety of water maintenance programs, including water main cleaning, valve turning, and hydrant operating.
Water main replacement programs were mostly completed as planned.
In 2023, we will continue with maintenance activities and the update of the Water Infrastructure Plan, or the WIP.
There are no concerns with the drinking water system.
Kitchener obtains treated water from the region of Waterloo and is responsible for the water
distribution system. The third report, the annual water quality report, is a compliance report to
confirm that we are taking enough samples, that we are reporting when outside the limits, and that
we are completing the appropriate corrective actions to resolve the issues. Kitchener is
audited annually by the Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks and is in compliance.
The Safe Drinking Water Act imposes a standard of care on every person who, on behalf of the municipality,
oversees the accredited operating authority of the system or exercises decision-making authority over the system.
You may have already taken a virtual training session as per the email that was sent earlier this year.
Taking care of your drinking water system, a guide for members of municipal councils,
is a document that outlines council responsibilities regarding the water system.
There is also a training session on March 21st.
There are three things to remember as a councillor.
It is your duty.
There are legal consequences including fines or imprisonment.
Be informed.
Your decisions have an impact on public health and be vigilant.
Don't take the drinking water safety for granted.
These reports assist in being informed and vigilant about the drinking water system.
